newsitem.title: IRAN: Snowstorm cuts off quake-hit Iranian villages.
newsitem.headline: Snowstorm cuts off quake-hit Iranian villages.

text.p: Heavy snow and blizzards have cut off roads to dozens of mountain villages in northwest Iran where tens of thousands of people were made homeless by an earthquake last week, state-run Tehran Radio said on Friday.

It said relief workers fought to open roads to 40 villages after one metre (three ft) of snow fell overnight in the rugged area on the slopes of Sabalan mountain where the highest peak reaches 4,811 metres (15,784 ft).

The snowstorm sent temperatures plummeting in the agricultural region where more than 36,000 people made homeless by the quake last Friday have been resettled in tents and other temporary shelters, the radio said.

Nearly 1,000 people were killed and 2,600 injured in the earthquake which hit Ardabil province, measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale. It was followed by 500 aftershocks and another quake measuring 5.2 on Sunday night.
More snow was forecast for the province which was Iran's coldest region with temperatures of minus eight degrees Celsius (17.6 Fahrenheit) in its capital, the city of Ardabil, it said.
Several countries have responded to Iran's appeal for international assistance through the United Nations.
Japan has pledged aid worth $300,000, Germany and the German Red Cross $235,000, Britain $200,000, Norway $90,000 and Denmark $35,000, said a U.N. report released in Tehran on Thursday.
The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), to which Iran belongs, was sending aid worth $300,000, it added.

Several U.N. agencies were contributing a total of $525,000 in aid and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies was giving 50,000 Swiss francs ($33,800) in addition to tents, blankets and food, the report said.
Iran has said aid was also coming from Turkey, Oman, Tunisia, Jordan, Azerbaijan and Saudi Arabia but it made no mention of the $25,000 the United States said it was donating.
